newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: RTRS-Bougainville says situation unchanged.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Bougainville says situation unchanged.

text.p: Bougainville Copper Ltd said on Wednesday the situation on the Papua New Guinea (PNG) island of Bougainville, where its Panguna copper mine has been closed since May 1989 by a secessionist rebellion, remains unchanged.

"Operation High Speed, a PNG defence force initiative against the BRA (Bougainville Revolutionary Army) rebels, was terminated and relations between the PNG defence force and BRA remain poor," the company said.
Bougainville Copper said one positive aspect of the current situation was that the people on the island were endeavouring to return to a form of normalcy.

"Some schools are open, people have moved out of the bush, and there is a growing number of groups and organisations maintaining an opposition to the continuing violence on Bougainville," the company said.

It said recent studies of alternative strategies for resumption of operations at Panguna had concentrated on minimising the time required to re-establish production after its return to the island and on reducing and spreading, over time, the total funding necessary.

"It is estimated that the total cost of returning the mine to full production will be at the upper end of the range of kina 400 million to kina 600 million (US$305 million to $457 million), spread over a number of years," Bougainville Copper said.
It said the resumption of operations at Panguna would only be possible following the achievement of a political resolution to the crisis.
"Accordingly, a strong consensus in favour of mining amongst the people of Bougainville is a prerequisite to any resumption of operations," the company said.

Bougainville Copper, which is 53.6 percent owned by RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd and 19.1 percent by the PNG government, has said initial production could start within 18 months of a decision to re-open the mine.
Bougainville Copper shares closed steady at 54 cents.
